## Summary

The May 10, 2026 [[stripe|Stripe]] guide describes real-time Radar evaluation for externally processed payments. The November 7 guide describes evaluation for any processor and adds a path for a separately evaluated payment later processed on Stripe. The business server calls `POST /v1/radar/payment_evaluations` to receive a PaymentEvaluation. The November diagram shows the server then transacting separately with the third-party processor. Evaluation provides risk information at any point in the payment lifecycle. The processor separately determines the transaction outcome.

## Signals and access

| Signal | Documented scope |
| --- | --- |
| `fraudulent_payment` | Default signal for payments likely to result in a fraud-coded dispute or early fraud warning. |
| `fraudulent_dispute` | Both captures describe predicting a dispute and blocking such payments with a fraudulent reason code. May labels this private preview. |
| `early_fraud_warning` | Predicts an early fraud warning. May labels this private preview. |

November omits the private-preview labels in the two signal headings and provides a form to request API access or additional capabilities. Approval and availability depend on the scope Stripe grants. The assessment response carries `recommended_action` and separate scores. The guide’s blocking language for `fraudulent_dispute` does not establish automatic blocking by the evaluation API at a third-party processor. See May lines 6–20 and November lines 7–37, 50–59 and 121–127.

## Evaluation inputs for non-Stripe payments

The May guide required a tokenized card PaymentMethod, a Radar Session and customer email. The November prerequisite section is specifically for non-Stripe payments and describes these routes.

- **Tokenized card.** The minimum PaymentEvaluation example supplies a card PaymentMethod, amount, currency, customer email and Radar Session. It omits a Stripe-Version header. The separately worded SAQ D condition concerns creating a PaymentMethod through the API.
- **Masked card.** The November guide requires separate approval and accepts the first six and last four digits with expiration details. Using these details instead of a tokenized PaymentMethod returns only `fraudulent_payment`. Its sample uses `2026-07-29.preview`.
- **Raw card.** The November guide requires both separate approval and PCI DSS compliance. It documents card number and expiry, with optional CVC, in the card details object. Its sample also uses `2026-07-29.preview`.
- **Device details and email.** Stripe recommends a Radar Session where possible. Direct device metadata in lieu of a Radar Session requires separate approval. Collect email using the PaymentMethod's `billing_details.email` or a Customer or customer-configured Account. The examples set `customer_details.email` on the evaluation. The guide also documents optional billing and shipping addresses.

See May lines 22–28 and November lines 39–48 and 61–133. The approval and version conditions belong to their specific routes.

## Result and score boundaries

Stripe returns `recommended_action` and a `signals` object containing each signal name, `evaluated_at`, `risk_level` and `score`. Predictions are scored independently. In the November multiprocessor guide, the fraudulent-payment categories are written as above 65 for elevated and above 75 for high. The blocking recommendation is 75 or above. The same-day [[raw/stripe-radar-transaction-risk-prevention-2026-11-07|Transaction Risk Prevention capture]] uses inclusive thresholds of 65 and 75 for the categories. Classification at the endpoints remains unresolved across these two guides (multiprocessor lines 121–127, transaction risk line 40).

## Stripe processing after a separate evaluation

November says Radar evaluates again by default when Stripe processes a payment that already had a separate PaymentEvaluation. Signals can change between evaluations, and both evaluations are billed. To avoid duplicate evaluations, the guide's `2026-07-29.preview` PaymentIntent confirm example sets `radar_options.payment_evaluation_options.skip_radar=true` and sends the prior evaluation IDs for the same payment. The guide describes including up to five evaluations or setting `skip_radar=false`. An evaluation ID already associated with another payment cannot be reused. The separate [[raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07|captured Confirm API reference]] lists optional `radar_options` at lines 627–631. The nested reuse options above are documented by the preview example (November multiprocessor lines 135–150).

November also documents sandbox keys and Radar test cards, idempotency keys for retries and expansion of related resources. Payment lifecycle reporting through the Payment Records API requires separate integration access (November lines 152–162).

radar-multiprocessor.text: Use Radar to evaluate your payments regardless of payment processor.
Use the form below to request access to the Payment Evaluation API or additional capabilities, including raw card details, masked card details, and direct client signals.
Any `PaymentEvaluation` created with these parameters instead of a `PaymentMethod` returns only the `fraudulent_payment` signal.
Stripe returns a response with the `recommended_action` property and the `signals` object.
You can’t use a `PaymentEvaluation` that has already been associated with another payment.
Evaluate your non-Stripe processed payments with Radar.

radar-multiprocessor.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/multiprocessor describes a business server requesting real-time Radar PaymentEvaluation risk signals for any processor, including Stripe, apart from actual processor execution. For non-Stripe payments, it documents a tokenized card PaymentMethod or approval-gated masked/raw card details, Radar Session or separately approved direct device details, and customer email. The minimum tokenized example shows the card PaymentMethod, amount, currency, customer email and Radar Session. Raw card use is PCI DSS gated and masked input yields only fraudulent_payment. Stripe returns recommended_action and independently scored signals (new raw lines 39-77 and 79-133). If a separate evaluation precedes Stripe processing, default processing evaluates again and both are billed; the guide’s preview example specifies how eligible prior evaluations for the same payment can be reused at confirmation (new raw lines 135-150). The revised source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor.md dates May's narrower non-Stripe tokenized card, Radar Session and email path (old raw lines 6-28) and retains the separately scoped November alternatives, version examples and billing and execution boundaries.
radar-multiprocessor.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/multiprocessor, November substantively adds processor breadth, access requests, approved card and client-input alternatives, risk-response details, duplicate evaluation and billing scope, and separate Payment Records access (new raw lines 7-47, 121-150 and 152-162). The revised source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor.md preserves the May non-Stripe scope and explicit private-preview labels for fraudulent_dispute and early_fraud_warning (old raw lines 6-28). November removes those heading labels and requires access, which does not establish general availability. The November multiprocessor guide gives category wording above 65 and above 75, and a blocking recommendation of 75 or above (new raw lines 121-127). The separate transaction-risk guide line 40 gives inclusive 65 and 75 for classification. Both dated captures describe fraudulent_dispute as blocking such payments, while the November sequence and response distinguish the processor transaction from Stripe's recommendation and scores (old raw line 16; new raw lines 15-17, 50-59 and 121-127). The evaluation response does not establish automatic blocking at another processor. The expanded text diagram is illustrative, and the form link routes to an access request. Retain the reciprocal Radar concept, separate Radar Sessions/PAYG/Payment Records routes, and review of both dated captures (old raw lines 22-31; new raw lines 39-59 and 152-162).

concept_suggestions.anchor:
## Multiprocessor (External Payment Evaluation)

Evaluate non-Stripe-processed payments with Radar at any point in the payment lifecycle. Signals: `fraudulent_payment` (default), `fraudulent_dispute` (preview, blocks), `early_fraud_warning` (preview). Prerequisites: tokenized PaymentMethod (card only) + Radar Session + customer email. API: `POST /v1/radar/payment_evaluations`. See [[source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor]].
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
## Multiprocessor Payment Evaluation

The May 2026 guide describes non-Stripe processing with a tokenized card, Radar Session and customer email. The November guide documents evaluations for any processor, approval-gated input alternatives for non-Stripe processing and a preview example for same-payment evaluation reuse when processing on Stripe. Both describe `fraudulent_payment` as the default and give blocking language for `fraudulent_dispute`. The response provides a recommendation and separate scores. The business server separately transacts with a third-party processor. See [[source-stripe-radar-multiprocessor]] for the dated signal, PCI and billing conditions.
